text: India's Chandrayaan-1 mission, launched in 2008, is credited with helping confirm the presence of what on the Moon?
explanation: Data from Chandrayaan-1, launched in 2008, provided key evidence of water molecules on the lunar surface.

text: India's Mars Orbiter Mission ('Mangalyaan') successfully entered Mars orbit in which year, making India the first Asian country to reach Mars?
explanation: Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit in September 2014, making ISRO the first Asian space agency to do so.

text: China's Chang'e 4 mission achieved the first-ever soft landing on which part of the Moon, in January 2019?
explanation: Chang'e 4 became the first spacecraft to land on the far side of the Moon, in January 2019.

text: SpaceX achieved the first successful landing of an orbital-class rocket's first stage in which year?
explanation: SpaceX first landed a Falcon 9 first stage successfully in December 2015, a milestone for reusable rockets.

text: In 2020, which company launched the first crewed orbital spaceflight from US soil since the Space Shuttle era, to the ISS?
explanation: SpaceX's Crew Dragon Demo-2 mission in May 2020 carried NASA astronauts to the ISS, the first crewed US orbital launch since 2011.

text: Aditya-L1, launched by India in 2023, is a mission to study which celestial body?
explanation: Aditya-L1 is ISRO's first dedicated mission to study the Sun, launched in September 2023.

text: The double-helix structure of DNA was described in 1953 by James Watson and which co-researcher?
explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick published the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953, drawing on X-ray data from Rosalind Franklin.

text: The Human Genome Project, which mapped nearly all human genes, was declared complete in which year?
explanation: The Human Genome Project was declared essentially complete in April 2003.

text: Dolly, the first mammal successfully cloned from an adult somatic cell, was born in which year?
explanation: Dolly the sheep was born in 1996 at the Roslin Institute in Scotland, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

text: Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic, was discovered by which scientist in 1928?
explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 after noticing mould inhibiting bacterial growth in his laboratory.

text: The World Wide Web was invented in 1989 by Tim Berners-Lee while working at which institution?
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN, the European particle physics laboratory.

text: Apple released the first iPhone in which year?
explanation: The first iPhone was released by Apple in June 2007.

text: The 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded for the development of which gene-editing technology?
explanation: Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing tools.

text: The first COVID-19 vaccine to receive widespread emergency authorisation, in December 2020, was developed by Pfizer in partnership with which company?
explanation: The Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine received emergency authorisation in December 2020, among the first in the world to do so.

text: Albert Einstein published his theory of general relativity in which year?
explanation: Einstein published his general theory of relativity in 1915, extending his 1905 special theory.

text: The periodic table of chemical elements, arranging elements by atomic weight and properties, was devised in 1869 by which scientist?
explanation: Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev published his periodic table of elements in 1869, successfully predicting undiscovered elements.

text: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in which year?
explanation: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901, five years after Alfred Nobel's death, per his will.

text: ARPANET, the precursor to the modern internet, transmitted its first message between computers in which year?
explanation: ARPANET sent its first host-to-host message in October 1969, between UCLA and Stanford Research Institute.

text: Pluto, discovered in 1930, was reclassified from a planet to a 'dwarf planet' by the International Astronomical Union in which year?
explanation: The IAU reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006 after defining stricter criteria for what constitutes a planet.

text: The Wright brothers achieved the first sustained, controlled, powered flight of an aircraft in which year?
explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright achieved the first powered flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, on 17 December 1903.

text: Which 19th-century French scientist developed the process of pasteurisation and advanced the germ theory of disease?
explanation: Louis Pasteur developed pasteurisation and provided key evidence for the germ theory of disease in the 19th century.

text: Marie Curie was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields. Which two?
explanation: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911.

text: Halley's Comet, one of the most famous periodic comets, returns to the vicinity of Earth approximately every how many years?
explanation: Halley's Comet has an orbital period of roughly 76 years; it was last visible from Earth in 1986 and is expected to return around 2061.

text: mRNA vaccine technology, long researched but never before approved for public use, was first deployed at scale during which event?
explanation: The COVID-19 pandemic saw the first large-scale approval and rollout of mRNA vaccines, developed by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, from late 2020.

text: Charles Darwin's 'On the Origin of Species', which introduced the theory of evolution by natural selection, was published in which year?
explanation: Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859, setting out the theory of evolution by natural selection.

text: Alexander Graham Bell was granted a patent for the telephone in which year?
explanation: Alexander Graham Bell received a patent for the telephone in 1876.
